rot.ideia.ex1.e1: There is a way for the game to end in a draw even with an extra queen: stalemate.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: The king is stalemated when it is his turn, he is not in check and he has no move at all.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: To see how it happens, do it on purpose: put the queen on a square that takes away all the king's moves, without giving check.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Stalemate the black king with the queen, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! The black king is not in check, but a7, b7 and b8 are all attacked.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The queen goes to b6 and reaches a7, b7 and b8, without attacking a8.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: After that move the black king still has somewhere to go. Let's go back: take away his three squares.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Stalemate the black king with the queen, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: It is Black's turn, and they have no move. The game ends in a draw.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: Remember the idea: no check and no move is stalemate, a draw. Check with no way out is mate.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Now the opposite: give checkmate, and be careful not to stalemate.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: The white king on c7 reaches b7 and b8. The queen still has to give check and close a7.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Give checkmate with the queen, without stalemating, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! Checkmate: the queen protected by the king, and the black king with no square.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The queen moves next to him on b7, protected by the king: checkmate.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.b1b6.1: Stalemate: the black king is not in check and has no move. It is a draw.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.b1b6.2: Let's go back: the move must give check.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.b1g1.1: Stalemate: the black king is not in check and has no move. It is a draw.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.b1g1.2: Let's go back: the move must give check.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not give check, and the black king escapes. Let's go back: look for the check.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Give checkmate with the queen, without stalemating, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: There were four mates: the queen on a1, a2, b7 or b8. They all give check.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Before a move that takes the king's squares, check: does it give check? If not, it is stalemate.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Now I will show two stalemates that often happen in games.
rot.demos.damaAfoga.e1: The black king is in the corner, on h8. It looks easy: the queen just has to come close.
rot.demos.damaAfoga.l1: The queen goes to f7, and the black king has no move, but no check. Stalemate: a draw.
rot.demos.damaAfoga.l2: Let's go back. The right move gives check along the last rank.
rot.demos.damaAfoga.l3: The queen goes to f8: check, and the white king on g6 reaches g7 and h7. Checkmate.
rot.demos.peaoAfoga.e1: Stalemate also saves the side that is losing. The white pawn is one square from becoming a queen.
rot.demos.peaoAfoga.l1: But it is Black's turn, and the king has no move: the pawn stands on a7 and reaches b8, and the white king reaches b7.
rot.demos.peaoAfoga.l2: No check and no move: a draw. The pawn never gets to become a queen.
rot.demos.peaoAfoga.l3: Now it's your turn: first giving mate without stalemating, then saving the draw with Black.
rot.pratica.mateSemAfogar.enunciado: Give checkmate with the queen, without stalemating the black king.
rot.pratica.mateSemAfogar.fim: Perfect. The move gave check, so it was mate, not stalemate.
rot.pratica.mateSemAfogar.err.c2c7: Stalemate: the black king has no move and no check. Try again.
rot.pratica.mateSemAfogar.err.c2h2: Stalemate: the black king has no move and no check. Try again.
rot.pratica.salvarEmpate.enunciado: Now you play Black. Take the king towards the corner on a8: there, he can be stalemated.
rot.pratica.salvarEmpate.fim: Well done. If the pawn moves up, the king goes to the corner on a8 and is stalemated: a draw.
rot.pratica.salvarEmpate.err.c8d7: The white king goes to b7, and the pawn becomes a queen. Try again: head for the corner.
rot.pratica.salvarEmpate.err.c8d8: The white king goes to b7, and the pawn becomes a queen. Try again: head for the corner.
